There is significant narrowing of the bronchial structures at the level of the left main bronchus due to mass-like conglomerate lymphadenopathies. In addition, multiple conglomerate lymph nodes are observed in the paraesophageal area, anterior diaphragmatic region, and around the celiac trunk. Impression:
Congenital hypoplasia of both lungs, prominent fibrotic recessions, and mass-like conglomerate lymphadenopathies obstructing the left bronchus; suggestive of primary lung malignancy with mediastinal and paraesophageal metastasis. Lytic bone lesion at T12 vertebral body.

Findings:

Upon examination of the lung parenchyma, multiple scattered areas of ground-glass opacity are noted bilaterally, predominantly in the peripheral distribution. Some of these opacities have central sparing, creating a "crazy paving" pattern. The pattern suggests pulmonary alveolar hemorrhage syndrome rather than organizing pneumonia (OP) or viral pneumonia. No pleural effusion or thickening is present. In addition, the presence of multiple pulmonary nodules with central necrosis and surrounding consolidation, along with ground-glass opacity, favors septic emboli over non-infectious causes such as OP or organizing pneumonia. There are also signs of volume loss, indicated by fissural thickening and elevation of the ipsilateral hilus. Minimal pleural effusions may be present in the fissures.

The upper abdominal organs within the field of view appear normal. There is no free air within the peritoneum. No ascites or peritoneal thickening is observed. The osseous structures show normal alignment, and there are no fractures. Degenerative changes, including osteophyte formation and disc space narrowing, are observed in the spine.

Impression:
Multiple scattered areas of ground-glass opacity with central sparing in both lungs, suggesting pulmonary alveolar hemorrhage syndrome rather than organizing pneumonia (OP) or viral pneumonia.
Presence of multiple pulmonary nodules with central necrosis and surrounding consolidation favors septic emboli rather than non-infectious causes like OP or organizing pneumonia (OP).
Signs of volume loss, minimal pleural effusions within the fissures, and degenerative changes in the spine.
